facts: CUSMA is a trade agreement among Canada, the United States and Mexico; the prior sourced packet describes cross-border production/trade.

The Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement is between Canada and the United States, first signed in 1972 and updated in 2012. Canada implements programmes and reports progress; the two countries coordinate restoration/protection priorities.
The water agreement’s reported structure includes cooperation with other governments, Indigenous peoples and local agencies; a commitment is not evidence all objectives have been met.
The Canadian Red Cross works with the Haitian Red Cross and other partners on humanitarian response, including the studied 2010 case.

Canada’s government reported supporting the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies and a Canadian–Norwegian Red Cross field hospital after the 2010 earthquake. These are distinct organizations/relationships, not a single Canadian government office.

MSF Canada describes recruiting professionals, raising resources and advocating in Canada to support the international medical-humanitarian movement. Its Canada office is not the government of Nepal or an international legislature.
After Nepal’s April 2015 earthquake, Canadian DART members supported Nepal-led relief. Reported work included medical care, filtration units and engineering/access support.

The mission history describes discussion with Nepalese authorities and a greater need for engineering road/rubble clearance than a standard purification deployment. Clearing routes helped assistance reach cut-off areas.

MSF reported mobile medical care, surgery, shelter materials, water storage and sanitation in affected Nepalese locations. Its activities and the government’s response were distinct, although both addressed disaster needs.
limits: Compare with Haiti 2010; do not merge the locations, dates, organizations or actual tasks.
Do not claim Canada led all relief, every NGO was governmental, or response outputs prove full long-term recovery.
